StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterCardExhausted.issue: RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30. Two divergences, BOTH now LIVE (this narrows a prior 'dormant only because' reading). (a) THE DRAW COUNT IS HARD-CODED TO 1. DarkEmbracePower.cs:47 draws `base.Amount`; powers.py:339 is still `DrawCmd.draw(self.owner, 1)`, ignoring `self.amount` entirely. The power's own StackType is Counter (Power.on_stack adds unconditionally, powers.py:64-66 not overridden here), and the sim's ONE ported applier (cards/dark_embrace_card.py:34, `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, DarkEmbracePower, 1, applier=ctx.player)`) always passes 1 -- but nothing stops a SECOND copy of the Dark Embrace card (an ordinary Rare Power card, not deck-unique; obtainable twice via separate card rewards across a run) from being played in the same combat, which stacks Amount to 2 via the additive Counter path. TRIGGER, named and executed by code-reading: play two copies of Dark Embrace in one combat, then exhaust any card -- C# draws 2, the sim still draws 1 (`DrawCmd.draw(self.owner, 1)` is a literal constant, not `self.amount`). (b) THE ETHEREAL DEFERRAL IS MISSING, and is independently live -- see the AfterSideTurnEnd entry, which is the same underlying mechanism as this hook's own dispatch site. FIX for (a): `DrawCmd.draw(self.owner, self.amount)`. RADIUS: shared with (b) -- fixing the draw amount alone still draws too early for an ethereal-caused exhaust; see AfterSideTurnEnd for the full fix. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30, LIVE, and one premise of the inherited text is now FALSE (STALE): the causedByEthereal PLUMBING this entry said 'cannot be fixed inside the power' now EXISTS. `hooks.on_card_exhausted(card, caused_by_ethereal: bool = False)` (hooks.py:914-928) and `Power.on_card_exhausted(self, card, caused_by_ethereal=False)` (powers.py:314-315, the base class) both carry the parameter today, dispatched with `caused_by_ethereal=True` from the sim's two ethereal-exhaust call sites (combat.py:709 and :730, `_process_turn_end_cards`) -- and joss_paper.py:47 already CONSUMES it (`if caused_by_ethereal:`), so the guard g2 finding ('the parameter does not exist on the sim's hook') is closed and recorded separately as faithful/stale. WHAT REMAINS, still real and still live: DarkEmbracePower.on_card_exhausted (powers.py:334-339) accepts the new parameter but does not branch on it -- it draws immediately regardless of `caused_by_ethereal`, instead of accumulating an etherealCount and deferring the draw to the side's end (DarkEmbracePower.cs:52-60, and the source comment at :18-23 explaining WHY: so the drawn cards survive the flush). EXECUTED ordering check: `combat.py:1260` calls `_process_turn_end_cards()` (where the ethereal exhaust + immediate draw happen) strictly BEFORE `combat.py:1272`'s `self.player.discard_hand(flush=...)` (the hand flush) inside `_end_turn_internal`. So a card Dark Embrace draws off a turn-end ethereal exhaust lands in the hand and is immediately discarded by the flush that follows in the same turn-end call -- exactly the bug the C# deferral exists to avoid. TRIGGER, named: Dark Embrace (ported card) + any ported Ethereal card left unplayed in hand at turn end (Apparition, or the ported ethereal curses/statuses Ascender's Bane / Clumsy / Dazed / Folly, all of which set `is_ethereal = True`). FIX: give DarkEmbracePower an `_ethereal_count` field; `on_card_exhausted` increments it and returns early when `caused_by_ethereal`; add an `after_player_turn_end` (or `on_enemy_side_end`, whichever slot lands after the flush) that draws `self.amount * self._ethereal_count` and resets the counter, mirroring the two-phase C# shape. RADIUS: shares dispatch machinery with the AfterCardExhausted entry's divergence (a) -- both live in the same method and a fix should address the amount and the deferral together. Cross-reference, NOT the same mechanism: turn_structure's Joss Paper gaps G4/G17 used to be cited here as the reason the parameter didn't exist; that plumbing is now shared infrastructure both Joss Paper and Dark Embrace consume, not a blocking dependency. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: `card.Owner.Creature != base.Owner` reduces to a tautology in the sim: there is one player, every Card belongs to it, and this power is only ever applied to the player. Same reading power_cmd's sim-entry note and SurroundedPower's own comment (powers.py:2574-2576) already record.

STALE, CLOSED as of today's tree (2026-07-30): the premise this guard was carried for -- 'the parameter does not exist on the sim's hook, so the branch cannot be taken' -- is now false. `caused_by_ethereal` is a real parameter on `Power.on_card_exhausted` (powers.py:314-315) and `HookSystem.on_card_exhausted` (hooks.py:914-928), dispatched `True` from both of the sim's ethereal-exhaust call sites (combat.py:709, :730) and already consumed by a different ported listener (relics/joss_paper.py:47, `if caused_by_ethereal:`). The branch CAN be taken inside a power today; DarkEmbracePower simply does not take it. That residual behaviour gap -- Dark Embrace ignores the flag and draws immediately instead of deferring -- is recorded once, on the AfterSideTurnEnd hook entry above, and not duplicated here to avoid two mechanism ids for one finding. WAS: 'The parameter does not exist on the sim's hook, so the branch cannot be taken. Carried as its own guard because it is the root of the AfterSideTurnEnd gap and a fix has to start here.'
